key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr combined the lowest measured wear rate with the best corrosion resistance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: For WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel, HVAF is a promising process choice when both wear and corrosion resistance are priorities.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, wear rates, and corrosion behavior.
Examined wear tracks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF reduced volume wear rate from (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for bare steel to (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) and showed the lowest corrosion current density among coatings, (1.75±0.02) µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
